Pepper · on-prem installation

Pepper Install Runbook

Steps for installing Pepper on a Linux VM that already runs Docker. Pepper runs as five containers from prebuilt images, so no source code or build is needed. Allow about 30 minutes. First, send us the answers to the questions in Information we need from you.

Pepper version__PEPPER_VERSION__
Install bundlepepper-install-__PEPPER_VERSION__.tar.gz
Imagesdocker.io/sundi133/pepper-api
docker.io/sundi133/pepper-worker
Web UI port3000/tcp

Information we need from you

Please send us answers to these before the install. Items marked if used only apply if you want that feature.

General

  1. What does uname -m print on the VM (x86_64 or aarch64)?
  2. What URL will Pepper have (for example https://pepper.yourcompany.local)? Do you have a TLS certificate for it, or a reverse proxy that terminates TLS?
  3. Can the VM reach Docker Hub and quay.io, directly or through a proxy? If not, we'll send an offline image archive.
  4. Is there an outbound proxy? Please send its address and the internal hosts that must bypass it.
  5. Which AI model endpoint should Pepper use (internal gateway, Azure OpenAI or other)? Is internet access allowed for it?
  6. Do your internal services use certificates from an internal CA? If so, please send the CA certificate (PEM).
  7. Are there files or folders whose content must never be sent to the AI model (for example production configuration)? Passwords, keys and tokens in code are masked automatically, and key files are never sent.
  8. How long may Pepper keep uploaded source code, scan history and the audit log? By default everything is kept.

Single sign-on (SAML)

  1. Which identity provider do you use (Microsoft Entra ID, ADFS, Okta, Ping, other)? If it is Entra ID, can we use OpenID Connect ("Sign in with Microsoft") instead of SAML? It is simpler to set up and handles users in many groups.
  2. Please register Pepper in your IdP with these values (replace <url> with the answer to General question 2):
    • Entity ID / Identifier: https://<url>/api/auth/saml/metadata
    • Reply URL / ACS: https://<url>/api/auth/saml/acs
    • Sign-on URL: https://<url>/api/auth/saml/login
    Once Pepper is running, you can also import our metadata from the Entity ID URL.
  3. Please send the IdP sign-on URL and the token-signing certificate (Base64).
  4. Does your IdP sign the whole response or only the assertion? Pepper requires at least one of them to be signed.
  5. Which claims carry the user's email, display name and group memberships? Please send the claim names, or confirm the standard ones.
  6. Which groups should map to which Pepper role (Admin, Security, Developer, Viewer)? For Entra ID, please send the group object IDs or app role values. Are any users members of more than 150 groups?
  7. Users who match none of those groups: should they get Viewer access, or be blocked from signing in?
  8. What session timeout do you require? When a user is removed in the IdP, Pepper blocks their next sign-in, but a session that is already open lasts until it expires. Automatic removal via SCIM is not supported. Is that acceptable?
  9. Should we keep one local password administrator as a break-glass account, and turn off self-registration?

Azure DevOps Server

  1. Which version do you run (2019, 2020, 2022 or 2022.1)?
  2. What is the exact server URL, including any virtual directory (for example https://tfs.yourcompany.local/tfs)? Which collections and projects should Pepper scan?
  3. Does the server use a certificate from an internal CA? If so, please send the CA certificate (PEM).
  4. Can the Pepper VM reach the server over HTTPS? On which port? Is there a proxy in between?
  5. Are personal access tokens (PATs) allowed? Please create one for a service account with these scopes:
    • Code (Read) to scan repositories
    • Code (Read & write) if Pepper should open fix pull requests
    • Pull Request Threads (Read & write) for pull request comments
    • Project and Team (Read)
    • Work Items (Read & write) if Pepper should create Azure Boards work items
    Who will rotate the PAT, and when does it expire?
  6. If used: should Pepper scan pull requests automatically? This needs a service hook from your server to Pepper's URL, secured with a shared Basic-auth password. Should a failed scan block merging through a branch policy?
  7. If used: should findings become Azure Boards work items? If so, which project, and which process template (Agile, Scrum, CMMI or Basic)? Which area and iteration paths? Which severities should be filed automatically? Which state should an item move to when Pepper no longer detects the issue?
  8. Do you have very large repositories, or repositories that use Git LFS?

Before you start

  • VM: Linux x86-64 (amd64). 4 vCPU and 16 GB RAM recommended (minimum 2 vCPU / 8 GB), 100 GB disk for Docker data.
  • Docker Engine 24 or newer with the Compose v2 plugin.
  • Outbound access from the VM, directly or through your proxy:
    • Docker Hub (registry-1.docker.io) and quay.io. Only needed to pull images; without it, use the offline route in step 4.
    • Your Git servers, for example Azure DevOps Server.
    • Your LLM endpoint.
    • api.osv.dev (optional, for dependency vulnerability data).
  • A DNS name for Pepper, for example pepper.yourcompany.local, and ideally a TLS certificate for it.
  • Commands below assume your user can run docker. If not, prefix them with sudo.
1

Check the VM

uname -m                                          # must print x86_64
docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'     # 24 or newer
docker compose version                            # Docker Compose version v2.x
df -h /var/lib/docker                             # at least 40 GB free
free -g                                           # 8 GB or more
2

Copy and unpack the install bundle

Copy pepper-install-__PEPPER_VERSION__.tar.gz to the VM (for example to your home directory), then:

sudo mkdir -p /opt/pepper && sudo chown "$USER" /opt/pepper
cd /opt/pepper
tar -xzf ~/pepper-install-__PEPPER_VERSION__.tar.gz --strip-components=1
ls -la          # docker-compose.yml  .env.example  setup.sh  INSTALL.md  RUNBOOK.html  certs/
3

Create the configuration

Create .env and fill in random secrets. Use hex values: a / or + in the database password would break its connection string.

cd /opt/pepper
cp .env.example .env && chmod 600 .env
sed -i "s|^NEXTAUTH_SECRET=.*|NEXTAUTH_SECRET=\"$(openssl rand -hex 32)\"|" .env
sed -i "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*|POSTGRES_PASSWORD=\"$(openssl rand -hex 24)\"|" .env
sed -i "s|^MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=.*|MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=\"$(openssl rand -hex 24)\"|" .env
sed -i "s|^ADMIN_PASSWORD=.*|ADMIN_PASSWORD=\"$(openssl rand -hex 12)\"|" .env

Now open .env (vi .env) and set these values:

SettingWhat to enter
NEXTAUTH_URLThe exact address users will open, for example https://pepper.yourcompany.local. For a first test without TLS: http://<vm-ip>:3000.
ADMIN_EMAILEmail for the first Pepper administrator.
LLM_PROVIDER
LLM_BASE_URL
LLM_MODEL
LLM_API_KEY		Your AI model endpoint. Examples for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, internal gateways and Ollama are in the comments of .env. You can change this later in the UI.

Every other setting is optional; see Configuration reference. Leave PEPPER_VERSION as __PEPPER_VERSION__. Keep a secure copy of .env: NEXTAUTH_SECRET encrypts stored credentials and can't be recovered.

grep -E '^(ADMIN_EMAIL|ADMIN_PASSWORD)=' .env     # the first sign-in
4

Start Pepper

cd /opt/pepper
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

The first start creates the database, which takes 1–3 minutes. Wait until it answers:

until curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/api/health; do echo "waiting..."; sleep 10; done
docker compose ps

Expected: all five services running, and pepper-api, postgres, redis and minio healthy.

The VM can't reach Docker Hub (offline route)

On any machine with internet access and Docker, download the images into one file:

V=__PEPPER_VERSION__
for i in docker.io/sundi133/pepper-api:$V docker.io/sundi133/pepper-worker:$V \
         postgres:16-alpine redis:7-alpine quay.io/minio/minio:latest; do
  docker pull --platform linux/amd64 "$i"
done
docker save -o pepper-images-$V.tar docker.io/sundi133/pepper-api:$V \
  docker.io/sundi133/pepper-worker:$V postgres:16-alpine redis:7-alpine quay.io/minio/minio:latest
sha256sum pepper-images-$V.tar > pepper-images-$V.tar.sha256

Copy both files to /opt/pepper on the VM, then load them and start without pulling:

cd /opt/pepper
sha256sum -c pepper-images-__PEPPER_VERSION__.tar.sha256
docker load -i pepper-images-__PEPPER_VERSION__.tar
docker compose up -d

If you run an internal registry (Harbor, Artifactory, Nexus), you can push the two Pepper images there instead. Then set PEPPER_API_IMAGE and PEPPER_WORKER_IMAGE in .env; see INSTALL.md section 3.

5

Open the port and sign in

Allow the web port through the VM firewall, if one is active:

# RHEL / Rocky / Alma
sudo firewall-cmd --add-port=3000/tcp --permanent && sudo firewall-cmd --reload
# Ubuntu / Debian
sudo ufw allow 3000/tcp

Open NEXTAUTH_URL in a browser and sign in with ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD. Then:

  1. Open Settings → LLM Config and click Test connection. The Data Sent to AI card there shows that secret masking is on and which files are never sent.
  2. Open Settings → Integrations and connect Azure DevOps (or GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket) with a personal access token.
  3. Run a first scan: New scan, pick a repository, Full scan.
6

Put HTTPS in front (recommended)

Point your existing reverse proxy or load balancer (nginx, IIS ARR, F5) at http://<vm>:3000, terminate TLS there, and allow long-lived responses, because scan progress is streamed. Then update the URL and restart:

cd /opt/pepper
sed -i 's|^NEXTAUTH_URL=.*|NEXTAUTH_URL="https://pepper.yourcompany.local"|' .env
echo 'PEPPER_BIND_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1' >> .env      # only if the proxy runs on this VM
docker compose up -d

An nginx example is in INSTALL.md section 4. Set proxy read timeouts to at least 1 hour and turn buffering off.

If your network needs it

Outbound proxy or internal certificate authority

Put your internal CA certificate (PEM) in /opt/pepper/certs/internal-ca.pem. Then add the lines you need to .env:

NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="/certs/internal-ca.pem"
GIT_SSL_CAINFO="/certs/internal-ca.pem"
HTTPS_PROXY="http://proxy.yourcompany.local:8080"
HTTP_PROXY="http://proxy.yourcompany.local:8080"
NO_PROXY="tfs.yourcompany.local,.yourcompany.local"

Apply with docker compose up -d. On SELinux-enforcing hosts, if the containers can't read the certificate, relabel the folder with sudo chcon -Rt container_file_t /opt/pepper/certs.

Azure DevOps Server (on-prem)

Set the REST API version that matches your server in .env, then connect it in Settings → Integrations → Azure DevOps with the server URL, collection and a PAT:

AZURE_DEVOPS_API_VERSION="7.0"     # 6.0 for Server 2020, 7.0 for Server 2022
Sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID

Register an app in Entra (single tenant). Use redirect URI https://pepper.yourcompany.local/api/auth/callback/entra and create a client secret. Then add to .env and run docker compose up -d:

ENABLE_ENTRA_SSO="true"
ENTRA_TENANT_ID="<directory-tenant-id>"
ENTRA_CLIENT_ID="<application-client-id>"
ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET="<client-secret>"
ENTRA_ROLE_MAP='{"Pepper.Admin":"ADMIN","Pepper.Security":"SECURITY","Pepper.Developer":"DEVELOPER"}'
ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION="false"

The role values are app roles you create on the Entra app registration. SAML is also supported; see the comments in .env.

Configuration reference (.env)

All settings live in /opt/pepper/.env. Only the first group is required. After any change run docker compose up -d; only the affected containers restart.

Required

SettingExamplePurpose
PEPPER_VERSION__PEPPER_VERSION__Pepper image tag. Change it only to upgrade.
NEXTAUTH_URLhttps://pepper.corp.localExact address users open, including https and any port.
NEXTAUTH_SECRETopenssl rand -hex 32Signs sessions and encrypts stored credentials. Never change it after setup; back it up.
POSTGRES_PASSWORDopenssl rand -hex 24Database password (hex only).
MINIO_ROOT_USER
MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD		pepper / hexObject storage credentials.
ADMIN_EMAIL
ADMIN_PASSWORD		First administrator, created on first start.

AI model

SettingDefaultPurpose
LLM_PROVIDERopenrouteropenai, azure, anthropic, custom (any OpenAI-compatible gateway), ollama …
LLM_BASE_URL
LLM_MODEL
LLM_API_KEY		Endpoint, model and key. Can also be changed later in Settings → LLM Config.
LLM_MASK_SECRETSnewtrueReplaces passwords, keys, tokens and connection-string passwords in code with placeholders before anything is sent to the model. Fix pull requests still contain the real values.
LLM_EXCLUDE_PATHSnew(none)Comma-separated globs of files never sent to the model, for example config/prod/**,*.tfvars. A pattern without / matches the file name anywhere. Key and keystore files (*.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, *.jks, id_rsa …) are always excluded. Rule-based scanners still scan these files.

Data retentionnew

SettingDefaultPurpose
UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYSforeverUploaded source archives are deleted this many days after upload (minimum 1). Scan results stay; rescanning that project asks for the archive again.
SCAN_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYSforeverScan history and finished AI fix runs older than this are deleted (minimum 30). Each project's latest scan is always kept.
AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYSforeverAudit entries older than this (minimum 30) are archived to object storage, then deleted. Can be overridden in Settings → Audit log.

Retention runs in the worker at most every 6 hours and records what it deleted in the audit log.

Day-to-day commands

cd /opt/pepper
docker compose ps                                   # status
docker compose logs -f pepper-api                   # web app logs
docker compose logs -f pepper-worker                # scan logs
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U pepper pepper | gzip > pepper-db-$(date +%F).sql.gz   # backup
docker compose down                                 # stop (data is kept)

A full backup has three parts: the database dump above, object storage (uploads, SBOMs, audit archives), and a secure copy of .env. Without the same NEXTAUTH_SECRET, stored credentials can't be decrypted after a restore.

cd /opt/pepper
docker run --rm -v pepper_miniodata:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/pepper-minio-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C /data .

To upgrade, back up the database, set the new PEPPER_VERSION in .env, then run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d. Database changes apply automatically.

If something doesn't work

SymptomWhat to check
"… is required in .env"A required setting is empty in .env.
pull: unauthorized / timeoutThe VM can't reach Docker Hub or quay.io. Check your proxy, or use the offline route in step 4.
pepper-api not healthydocker compose logs pepper-api. Usually disk space or a changed database password.
Sign-in loops backNEXTAUTH_URL must match the browser address exactly.
Scans stay "Queued"docker compose logs pepper-worker
Clone fails / x509 errorsProxy and NO_PROXY, or the internal CA settings above.

To get help, send us the output of these two commands. Neither prints your secrets.

cd /opt/pepper
docker compose ps > pepper-status.txt
docker compose logs --tail 300 pepper-api pepper-worker > pepper-logs.txt
